Report_ID: Cure ratio (proportion of children discharged from OTP as cured)
Title: The effectiveness of treatment for Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) delivered by community health workers compared to a traditional facility based model
Author: Alvarez Morán et al.
Comment: Two RRs are reported for the same outcome: the Abstract's unadjusted risk ratio 1.07 (95% CI 1.01; 1.13), recorded here in the ratio fields because it is directly consistent with the raw counts (581/617 vs 187/212), and Table 6's RR 1.89 (95% CI 1.09-3.27, p=0.022) which is adjusted for sex, oedema and MUAC at admission. The p-value recorded (0.022) comes from the adjusted Table 6 analysis. Abstract states the control cure ratio as 88.6% whereas Table 6 reports 88.2% (187/212). Denominators are children discharged from OTP, not all admitted (699 vs 235); non-respondents were not recorded in the control group (set to zero), so denominators are not perfectly comparable. Allocation was by geographic area (clustered); no ICC is reported by the trial.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Intervention area: SAM treatment delivered by Community Health Workers (plus 3 health centres)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
domain: child nutrition / severe acute malnutrition treatment delivery
Participant type: Children aged 6-59 months with uncomplicated severe acute malnutrition
Recruitment source: Kita district health facilities and community health workers, Kayes region, Mali
Outcome measurement: Number cured / number discharged from OTP in each arm
Outcome variable: Cure ratio (proportion of children discharged from OTP as cured)
additional_group_ns: Admitted (ITT): intervention 699, control 235; discharged from OTP: intervention 617, control 212

Title: Effectiveness of screening and treatment of children with severe acute malnutrition by community health workers in Simiyu region, Tanzania: a quasi-experimental pilot study
Author: Wilunda et al.
Comment: Non-randomised, ward/district-level allocation (clustered design) but the paper reports no ICC and no cluster-adjusted analysis; RRs come from individual-level Poisson regression with robust error variances. Control denominator 148 is the complete-case (missing outcomes excluded) analysis matching the extracted adjusted RR (N = 358); the multiply imputed ITT analysis (control 116/154 = 75.3%) gave adjusted RR 1.18 (95% CI 1.05, 1.32). Unadjusted RR was 1.20 (1.08, 1.32). The reported RR is adjusted for wealth index, HIV exposure and fever.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Intervention: uncomplicated SAM treated at home by community health workers with RUTF (Bariadi district wards)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
domain: child nutrition / community management of severe acute malnutrition
Participant type: Children aged 6–59 months with severe acute malnutrition (MUAC < 11.5 cm) without medical complications
Recruitment source: Community screening by CHWs (intervention wards, Bariadi district) and health facility enrolment by formal health workers (control wards, Maswa district), Simiyu Region, Tanzania
Outcome measurement: Number and proportion of children cured per arm; risk ratio from Poisson regression with robust error variances, adjusted for wealth index, HIV exposure and fever

Report_ID: Proportion of children cured (absence of oedema and WHZ ≥ 1.5 and/or MUAC > 125 mm during two consecutive weeks)
Title: Effectiveness and Coverage of Treatment for Severe Acute Malnutrition Delivered by Community Health Workers in the Guidimakha Region, Mauritania
Author: Charle-Cuéllar et al.
Comment: Denominators (496, 209) are children with KNOWN treatment outcome, not the ITT numbers treated (618 intervention, 251 control); outcome was unknown for 122 intervention and 42 control children. The reported effect measure is a time-adjusted hazard ratio from Cox regression, not a risk ratio. The intervention arm is a mixed-delivery zone (HF or CHW), not a pure lay-worker arm. No ICC reported for the facility/commune cluster structure.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Intervention zone (outpatient SAM treatment from health facilities OR community health workers; 10 HF, 12 CHWs)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: Children aged 6–59 months with uncomplicated severe acute malnutrition
Recruitment source: Health facilities, CHW sites, community volunteer screening and mobile clinics in Guidimakha region
Outcome measurement: Number and percentage of children discharged as cured, among children with known treatment outcome
Outcome variable: Proportion of children cured (absence of oedema and WHZ ≥ 1.5 and/or MUAC > 125 mm during two consecutive weeks)
unit_of_analysis: per participant (child with known treatment outcome)

Report_ID: Recovery from severe acute malnutrition (recovered: oedema resolved and final weight-for-height >85% of ideal)
Title: A large-scale operational study of home-based therapy with ready-to-use therapeutic food in childhood malnutrition in Malawi
Author: Linneman, Matilsky, Ndekha, Manary, Maleta & Manary
Comment: No p-value, risk ratio, confidence interval or ICC was reported for this comparison — the paper only states 'there were no differences'. Counts are raw, from a non-randomised comparison in which each centre self-selected its staffing model; children are clustered within centres (3 lay-worker centres, 5 professional centres), so cluster adjustment with an assumed ICC would be required downstream. The intermediate 'referred by professionals, cared for by community health aids' arm (670/738) was excluded as it does not map cleanly to either plan arm.
Design Type: non-randomised operational cohort with centre-level (clustered) staffing-model comparison; no concurrent randomised control
domain: child nutrition / treatment of acute malnutrition
Study Environment: field / operational programme in rural sub-Saharan Africa
Participant type: Children aged 6-60 months with severe malnutrition (98% kwashiorkor) and good appetite, 12 rural centres in southern Malawi
Recruitment source: Children presenting to 12 rural treatment centres (district hospitals, mission hospitals, rural health centres), May 2005 - May 2006
Outcome measurement: Number (%) of severely malnourished children categorised as 'recovered' out of all children treated, by staff organization/formal medical training
Outcome variable: Recovery from severe acute malnutrition (recovered: oedema resolved and final weight-for-height >85% of ideal)
additional_group_ns: Excluded third/intermediate arm: children referred by medical professionals but cared for by community health aids, 670/738 (91%) recovered (4 centres) — not used because delivery responsibility is mixed across cadres

Report_ID: Cured (proportion of children discharged as cured) — intervention commune (HFs + CHWs) vs control commune (HFs only)
Title: Impact of Integration of Severe Acute Malnutrition Treatment in Primary Health Care Provided by Community Health Workers in Rural Niger
Author: Dougnon AO, Charle-Cuéllar P, Toure F, Aziz Gado A, Sanoussi A, Lazoumar RH, Tchamba GA, Vargas A, Lopez-Ejeda N
Comment: p value reported as "<0.001"; recorded as 0.001. Hazard ratio is from Cox regression adjusted by admission criteria (WHZ, MUAC, both or edema), reference = control group — it is not a risk ratio; RR should be computed from the cure counts/totals. The intervention arm mixes CHW-delivered and facility-delivered treatment (39.2% of intervention children treated by CHWs). Non-randomized, commune-level (cluster) allocation; no ICC reported.
Participant type: Children aged 6–59 months with uncomplicated severe acute malnutrition
Recruitment source: Health facilities and CHW health huts in two rural communes of Mayahi health district, Maradi region, Niger
Outcome measurement: Proportion cured out of children admitted to outpatient treatment per study group
Outcome variable: Cured (proportion of children discharged as cured) — intervention commune (HFs + CHWs) vs control commune (HFs only)
unit_of_analysis: per participant (child admitted to outpatient treatment)
